name: Paths on the Tree
description: You are given a rooted tree consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices. The vertices are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, and the root is the vertex $$$1$$$. You are also given a score array $$$s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n$$$. A multiset of $$$k$$$ simple paths is called valid if the following two conditions are both true. Each path starts from $$$1$$$. Let $$$c_i$$$ be the number of paths covering vertex $$$i$$$. For each pair of vertices $$$(u,v)$$$ ($$$2\le u,v\le n$$$) that have the same parent, $$$|c_u-c_v|\le 1$$$ holds. The value of the path multiset is defined as $$$\sum\limits_{i=1}^n c_i s_i$$$. It can be shown that it is always possible to find at least one valid multiset. Find the maximum value among all valid multisets.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le k \le 10^9$$$) — the size of the tree and the required number of paths. The second line contains $$$n - 1$$$ space-separated integers $$$p_2,p_3,\ldots,p_n$$$ ($$$1\le p_i\le n$$$), where $$$p_i$$$ is the parent of the $$$i$$$-th vertex. It is guaranteed that this value describe a valid tree with root $$$1$$$. The third line contains $$$n$$$ space-separated integers $$$s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_n$$$ ($$$0 \le s_i \le 10^4$$$) — the scores of the vertices. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10 ^ 5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print a single integer — the maximum value of a path multiset.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1746D — Paths on the Tree [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
